sections.h2: Where is Habersham County and what lies inside it?
sections.html:
Habersham County fills a corner of northeast Georgia in the Blue Ridge, with Clarkesville as the county seat and Cornelia as its biggest city. It was chartered on December 15, 1818, and takes its name from Colonel Joseph Habersham, who served in the Continental Army. Statistically the whole county forms the Cornelia, GA micropolitan area (Wikipedia).

The county measures 279 square miles, 277 of them land, and a share of the Chattahoochee National Forest falls within it. The top elevation is a knob around 4,400 feet just below the summit of Tray Mountain, which Habersham divides with White and Towns counties, with the Appalachian Trail following the ridge close by. The Chattahoochee River rises in what used to be Habersham County, a point Sidney Lanier's poem about the river makes with its line about the hills of Habersham.

Habersham once spread across much of northeast Georgia. White and Lumpkin counties took land from it in 1857, Banks County in 1859 and Stephens County in 1905. Rabun, Stephens, Banks, Hall, White and Towns counties now touch it, along with Oconee County, South Carolina. Raoul is a census-designated place, while Batesville, Habersham Mills, Hollywood and Turnerville are unincorporated communities. Public schooling comes from one system, the Habersham County School District, and Tallulah Falls School, Piedmont University and North Georgia Technical College are also located here.

sections.h2: What does Census data show for Habersham County?
sections.html:
The 2020 count was 46,031 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 50,416 means growth of 9.5%. About 20.3% of residents are 65 or older, and 9.4% were born abroad.

Over the long run the numbers climb steadily. Habersham had 3,145 residents in 1820, 18,116 in 1960, 35,902 in 2000 and 43,041 in 2010 before the 2020 count of 46,031, according to Wikipedia's table of census results. Owner-occupants hold close to three of every four homes, and 390 permits in 2025 show new building joining a digest of mostly older property. The commissioner's page says the appraisal staff sets values using recent sales and market conditions on January 1, so a house's figure can follow neighborhood sales (QuickFacts).

sections.h2: Who does what in Habersham County property tax?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner holds an elected constitutional office, sending bills, collecting, accounting for and disbursing the money, and takes no part in setting values or rates. Values are the job of the Board of Tax Assessors, which started in 1968 with three members and has had five since January 1, 1990, each serving a three-year term. Rates are set by the county commissioners and the school board, while the state's own levy cannot go beyond one-fourth of a mill.

  • Tax commissioner: 130 Jacobs Way, Suite 202, Clarkesville, GA 30523, phone (706) 839-0120, open on weekdays from 8:00 until 4:45, with Saturdays closed until further notice.
  • Tax assessors: phone (706) 839-0100, the number the county gives for mobile home registration questions.
  • Board of Tax Assessors meetings: second and fourth Mondays monthly, beginning at 9 a.m.

The assessors' board has a long to-do list that matters to sellers: it decides which properties are exempt, approves or denies Conservation Use applications and homestead exemptions, reviews tax returns, and levies penalties against property that was never returned. It also meets with taxpayers to talk through concerns, so a seller who doubts a value can ask for that conversation before listing.

Further detail sits on the commissioner's information page and the assessors' board page.

sections.h2: Which dates drive a Habersham County tax bill?
sections.html:
The commissioner's page names August 15 as the mailing target and November 15 as the payment date, both in the same year. That is earlier than the state default of December 20. Mobile and modular homes use a different cycle, since their bills usually go out around February 1 and the tax and location permit are tied to April 1.

Missing the April 1 payment and permit on a mobile home brings a 10% penalty, a citation to appear in the county's Magistrate Court, and in the end possibly a sale of the home. A decal has to be displayed, and registration is done through the assessors' office.

sections.h2: How does a Habersham County assessment appeal proceed?
sections.html:
Spring is when assessment notices normally arrive, and an unhappy owner then has 45 days from the date on the notice. The written appeal may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, and it goes to the Board of Tax Assessors naming the method you have picked.

Mobile homes carry an extra step on this page: if the owner still disagrees after a changed value, the county says an appeal to the Board of Equalization can follow within 21 days of that notice. That board is appointed by the grand jury and exists to hear administrative appeals from the assessors' values. For a regular parcel, ask the assessors' office for forms and the exact sequence.

sections.h2: Which Habersham County exemptions and special valuations should I know about?
sections.html:
Homestead applications are handled by the Tax Assessor's office, and new buyers should carry in the warranty deed. Filing by April 1 covers your first claimed year, and a late filing slides to the following year. After approval the exemption renews itself until your residence, ownership or qualifying category changes. The county reports local exemptions that take the place of state ones whenever the local amount is greater.

  • Land in genuine agricultural use can be assessed at 30% rather than 40% of fair market value.
  • Conservation Use valuation is granted in return for a covenant with the assessors to keep the land in qualifying use for ten years at least.
  • Freeport exemption for manufacturers can reach three categories: raw goods, goods being processed, and finished goods held in a warehouse for out-of-state shipment; applications are filed between January 1 and April 1.
  • A business's equipment, machinery and fixtures are assessed at 40% of fair market value.

sections.h2: What should a Habersham County seller do when tax is still due?
sections.html:
Georgia holds the January 1 owner responsible for the whole year and refunds nothing for a partial year. The sale contract normally decides who actually pays, so begin by learning the precise balance.

Phone the tax commissioner at (706) 839-0120 and ask what the parcel owes for this year and any before it. When closing lands between the August mailing and the November 15 date, let the closing agent know whether the new bill has gone out and been paid. A mobile home bill follows the April 1 cycle and stands apart from real property. A homestead exemption ends when you move or ownership changes, so tell the assessors after you leave and let the buyer file separately.

faqs.q: What day is Habersham County property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed by August 15 and payment is expected by November 15. For mobile and modular homes, bills typically go out near February 1 and the tax is tied to April 1.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Habersham County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: The Main Office is at 130 Jacobs Way, Suite 202, Clarkesville, GA 30523, phone (706) 839-0120. Weekday hours end at 4:45, starting at 8:00, and Saturdays are closed until further notice.

faqs.q: What is the time limit to appeal a Habersham County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the notice. A written appeal naming your chosen method goes to the Board of Tax Assessors.

faqs.q: By when must a Habersham County homestead application arrive?
faqs.a: April 1 in the first year you claim. Take the application to the Tax Assessor's office, with your warranty deed if the purchase is recent.

faqs.q: Is farmland taxed differently in Habersham County?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Qualifying agricultural property is assessed at 30% of fair market value, not 40%, and Conservation Use valuation applies current-use value in exchange for a covenant of ten years or longer with the assessors.
